analysis.title: The Flow Show: From Johnny Lovedrop to Billy Big Boots
key_insights: The Flow Show returns December 3rd after the US Thanksgiving break. YTD returns through 11/18: oil +44.9%, US dollar +5.7%, US stocks +4.8%, global stocks +4.4%, cash +3.3%, HY -1.2%, IG -3.0%, govt bonds -3.9%, gold -15.1%, bitcoin -29.5%.

The 30-year US Treasury is on course for a 6th straight year of negative price return, the longest streak since 1963-69. The GT30 yield is 25bps below its recent high while Nasdaq is -15%, banks -16% and oil -22% from highs. BofA asks why there is no Q4 release valve for risk assets, and argues yields are more likely to rise than fall in the next recession because debt levels are too high.

The key question for markets is when rate hikes end. If the Fed still treats the stock market as too big to fail, a credit and stock slump (IG CDX above 80bps, SPX below 6845, which would erase YTD gains) would short-circuit the hiking cycle. If the Fed is now an inflation fighter after the midterms, hard landing risks grow, and the March 18 and April 28 FOMC meetings are the earliest investors can price the end of the cycle.
Signals for peak hike fears: a top in the US dollar, and lows in bitcoin, gold and KOSPI, which BofA says were the first assets to anticipate hikes.

BofA sees the market as 'post-bubble', comparing it to 2000 when tech peaked in March, then slumped while utilities, staples and healthcare rallied as the Fed hiked 100bps. In 2001 Fed hikes caused a recession and a bear market. The dollar was very strong in both years, and the Nasdaq had 12 bear market rallies above 10% within the bear market.

Soft landing case: if lower inflation, stable employment and higher productivity are visible by spring and EPS growth holds above 10%, then SPX below 7000 is a buy. SPW trades at 16x forward P/E, mid caps at 15x and ACWI ex-US at 12x. BofA would then buy cyclicals (crypto, chips, copper, consumer, condos) once the narrative flips from hikes to cuts.

BofA's own view is that hard landing odds are too low in consensus and consensus 'boom' forecasts (5-6% nominal GDP, above 15% EPS in 2027) are too high. US household equity wealth is down about $5tn QTD, though still up about $8tn in 2026. Hyperscalers forecast $1.3tn capex in 2027 against -$283bn free cash flow.

Recession tells: jobless claims above 250k and IG spreads above 100bps would signal the 'boom loop' has turned into a 'doom loop', forcing allocators to cut stocks and move to bonds, China, the US dollar and assets negatively correlated with AI (REITs and real estate, 'long condos, short chips').

Weekly flows (week ended 11/18): $66.6bn into stocks ($73.5bn to ETFs, $6.8bn out of mutual funds), $0.4bn to cash, $0.2bn to gold, $1.1bn out of crypto, $7.4bn out of bonds. Bond outflow was the first since Apr'25. EM debt saw a $7.5bn outflow, the biggest since Apr'20. US growth stocks took $9.1bn, the biggest since Dec'24. Tech had an 8th week of inflows ($5.4bn).

BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.1 from 7.4 (signal Neutral), driven by outflows from EM debt and HY bonds, wider HY and subordinated bank spreads, worse equity breadth and more bearish futures positioning. FMS positioning and equity flow components are at extreme bullish readings (100th and 99th percentile) while global stock index breadth is very bearish (18th percentile).

Nov FMS: only 3% of investors expect a hard landing (50% soft, 42% no landing), cash is at 3.6% and there was a record $310bn inflow to equity funds and ETFs over 4 weeks. BofA says price capitulation has occurred but it needs more positioning capitulation before an all-clear to buy risk.

BofA Global Breadth Rule: net 68% of global equity indices are oversold, against the 88% needed for the contrarian buy signal. BofA expects it to trigger in coming days, giving short-term relief after Thanksgiving, but a bigger rally needs the 10-year UST yield below 4.5%, WTI below $70 and a dollar top on weak payrolls or CPI.

Nov FMS positioning heading into 2027: overweight stocks, commodities, EM, healthcare and industrials; underweight cash, bonds, REITs, consumer and energy. Investors expect international stocks (36%) and US stocks (24%) to be the best asset classes in 2027. Targets: 10-year UST 4.9%, EURUSD 1.12, S&P 500 7926, gold $4341.

2026 record inflows: global equities ($1.5tn annualized), global bonds ($909bn), US stocks ($751bn), US large cap ($669bn), IG bonds ($443bn), Treasuries ($243bn), tech funds ($229bn), Korea stocks ($79bn). Record outflow from consumer funds (-$20bn).

BofA private clients ($4.6tn AUM) hold 65.7% stocks, 17.7% bonds and 9.4% cash. They bought bank loan, TIPS and HY bond ETFs over 4 weeks and sold utilities, consumer discretionary and energy ETFs. Equity ETF share count is up 1.1% over 4 weeks and 9.5% YTD.
Best 2026 trades: long oil-short crypto, long energy-short discretionary, long semis-short telecom, long small cap value-short mega cap growth, long Taiwan-short China, long cyber-short defense.

BofA would buy them once the narrative flips from rate hikes to cuts, not before.

tension_points.bear_case: If the Fed is now an inflation fighter after the midterms, hard landing risks grow and the March 18 and April 28 FOMC meetings are the earliest markets can price peak rates.
